response.sql: WITH state_counts AS (SELECT c.state_county_province AS state, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Accounts a JOIN Customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.state_county_province), shares AS (SELECT state, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM state_counts) AS share FROM state_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_s FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS combined_count, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - av.avg_s) AS avg_excess_over_overall_average FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share av WHERE s.share > av.avg_s

assumptions.assumption: The count per state is the number of accounts (rows of Accounts inner-joined to Customers), not the number of distinct customers.
NULL state_county_province values form a single group (GROUP BY puts NULLs together); empty strings are kept as their own distinct group.
The 'average share' in the output is the average of the shares of the qualifying states only, while the overall average share (the threshold) is computed across all states.
